paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the gospel Paul preached was the real thing, and nobody had to add to it. Paul laid it out in front of the leaders in Jerusalem, and they "added nothing" to him (Galatians 2:6). Even Titus, a Greek, was not "compelled to be circumcised" (Galatians 2:3). Christ alone is enough, and that is still good news today.

Now, some people will always show up wanting to add a little something extra. Paul says the false brothers came in to "spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us" (Galatians 2:4). He says, "We did not give in to them for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel would remain with you" (Galatians 2:5). Friend, that means the gospel is worth protecting, and holding it firmly is a kindness to the people who come after you.

And look how the whole thing lands. The leaders saw that the same One was at work in Peter and in Paul (Galatians 2:8), so they gave Paul and Barnabas "the right hand of fellowship" (Galatians 2:9). Different roads, same God, same gospel, and God "does not show favoritism" (Galatians 2:6). They asked only that they remember the poor, "the very thing I was eager to do" (Galatians 2:10). So here's your takeaway: hold tight to the gospel, make room for others who serve Christ, and let love for people in need show that the gospel has really taken hold.
